subject.title: fix: keep exec approval carriers scoped [AI]

question: Should bare `command`, `builtin`, and `exec` be unwrapped at this trust-plan boundary for every non-Windows argv input, or only when the caller can prove the argv originated from POSIX shell carrier syntax?
rationale: This is an authorization-classification contract: the correct answer depends on the producer and provenance guarantees of the argv reaching this module, which cannot safely be inferred from the supplied partial diff alone.

options.title: Require shell provenance before unwrapping
options.body: Restrict carrier unwrapping to argv produced by the documented POSIX shell parsing path, preserving direct executable invocations as literal executables.

options.title: Accept bare-token carrier semantics
options.body: Keep the PR's current behavior if the exec-approval contract guarantees that all matching bare tokens represent POSIX carrier syntax at this boundary.

recommendation.title: Require shell provenance before unwrapping
recommendation.body: Restrict carrier unwrapping to argv produced by the documented POSIX shell parsing path, preserving direct executable invocations as literal executables.
